messages:
rachel: Heads-up: release build of the Android sample app is failing to stream tokens on some devices (only repro in release, debug works).
rachel: Repro steps: build release APK (R8 enabled) -> start chat stream -> no tokens arrive, UI spinner stays forever. Works on emulator and debug APK. Pixel 5 & OnePlus 9 repro.
tom: curious. Any stack traces in Logcat? R8 can strip okio/Retrofit primitives if proguard rules missing.
rachel: Logcat is sparse, but I see: 
```
E/AndroidRuntime: java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: No virtual method getBuffer()Lokio/Buffer;
```
rl: (typo!)
lee: that smells like mixed okhttp/okio versions at runtime (maybe platform-provided vs bundled). Release build might be doing class merging and some okhttp classes are renamed/removed.
android-oncall: tagging: @android-oncall can you check our sampleapp proguard rules? We ship a suggested consumer-proguard-rules in the SDK aar.
android-oncall: taking a look. Which SDK artifact and gradle settings? rachel: using com.redwood:inference-android:1.4.0, minifyEnabled true, shrinkResources true.
tom: Our README suggests adding `-keep class okhttp3.** { *; }` but the SDK aar should include consumer rules. Maybe gradle isn't merging them because of variant mismatch.
rachel: confirmed: the aar has proguard.txt but consumerRules aren't merged in our app because we use component publishing? will open a quick build inspect.
lee: while investigating, try adding explicit rules to app/proguard-rules.pro: 
```
-keep class okhttp3.** { *; }
-keep class okio.** { *; }
-keepattributes Signature
-keepclassmembers class okhttp3.internal.ws.RealWebSocket { *; }
```
This fixed a similar issue last year.
devex-bot: Note: sampleapp CI (release) skipped proguard checks; enabling now for this branch.
build-bot: CI: sampleapp:ReleaseIntegration - failed: StreamReleaseTest.testReleaseStreaming - hung after 120s. See https://ci.redwood/test/12999
android-oncall: fwiw, if okhttp is getting shadowed by platform okhttp on some OEM firmware, you can force shading or add package relocation. Alternatively ensure the SDK bundles okio + okhttp with unique package names.
rachel: quick workaround: added those keep rules, rebuilt release APK and streaming resumed on Pixel 5. However still seeing occasional truncated streams (partial tokens then closed). Log shows HTTP/2 stream reset: 
```
I/OkHttp: <--- HTTP/2 200 (stream=13)
W/OkHttp: stream failed: java.io.EOFException: source exhausted prematurely
```
tom: EOFException can happen if the server closes stream unexpectedly OR if the client mis-handles chunked/streaming response body due to interceptor changing buffer. Any custom network interceptors?
rachel: sampleapp uses a debug interceptor that logs body when ENABLE_DEBUG true. But that shouldn't run in release. Strange.
lee: check that debug logging flag isn't accidentally true in release config via BuildConfig merge. Also R8 can inline constants differently, causing a debug flag to be true if not kept.
tom: good point. Ensure debug constant is final and obfuscated as expected or control via resources.
rachel: I changed logging flag and redeployed: less truncation. Root cause seems twofold: missing proguard rules causing okhttp/okio method mismatches + a debug logging interceptor enabled in release due to build config quirk.
android-oncall: action items: 1) Ensure SDK AAR consumer proguard rules are published and merged for all variants. 2) Update sampleapp README with explicit proguard snippet and note to validate BuildConfig booleans. 3) Add a unit/instrumentation release-mode test to CI to catch R8-related streaming regressions. I'll file ENG-4599.
lee: I'll open a PR to add the keep rules to the sampleapp and add a Gradle check that consumer proguard files are merged.
build-bot: PR job: https://ci.redwood/p/lee/proguard-fix - running tests.
devex-bot: FYI: UX note: onboarding guide should highlight "release build streaming checklist" (proguard rules, debug flags, okhttp version).
tom: long-term: consider shading okhttp/okio in the SDK to avoid platform conflicts. Requires coordination with size budgets.
rachel: thanks all. I'll validate on Pixel 5 and OnePlus 9 once PR merges and update here. Leaving trace link: https://logs.redwood/internal/streaming/repro/1991234567
